questions.text: What are Steering files in Kiro?

options.label: Persistent Markdown knowledge about the project, such as patterns, decisions, and conventions that guide the agent
Automations that trigger agent actions when IDE events occur, like saving a file
Installable packages that bundle documentation and MCP servers to expand Kiro
Specification documents that define requirements, design, and tasks for a feature

questions.explanation: Steering gives Kiro persistent project knowledge in Markdown files: architecture, patterns, decisions, vocabulary, and other conventions. The inclusion mode determines when each file enters the context.

questions.text: Steering files can be defined both at the user level (~/.kiro/steering/) and at the workspace level (.kiro/steering/).
questions.explanation: Steering files can exist at two levels: in the user directory (~/.kiro/steering/) for personal settings, and in the workspace (.kiro/steering/) for settings shared with the team via version control.

questions.text: Your team wants Kiro to always follow a specific pattern when creating React components. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.label: Create a Steering file in the workspace with the team's component conventions
Create a Skill with the conventions and ask each developer to activate it manually before creating components
Configure a Hook that rewrites the component to match the standard every time a file is saved
Document conventions in a root README and trust that Kiro reads it automatically in every task

questions.explanation: A file in `.kiro/steering/` can be versioned with the project. To apply the rule in every interaction, set `inclusion: always` in its front matter; other modes load it only by match, relevance, or manual reference.

questions.text: You want a Steering file included automatically when the user's request is semantically relevant, even when no matching file is open. Which configuration should you use?

options.label: `inclusion: auto`, with a `name` and `description` that help Kiro decide relevance
`inclusion: fileMatch`, without `fileMatchPattern`, so Kiro infers semantically related files
`inclusion: always`, because that mode loads the file only when its description matches the request
`inclusion: manual`, with a description; Kiro will reference it automatically when needed

questions.explanation: The `auto` mode uses `name` and `description` so Kiro can decide semantically when the content is relevant. The other current modes are `always`, `fileMatch`, and `manual`.
